### Air track AIR-3 - the lit march: the light-in-air march reads the fog grid - 2026-10-27
Branch `track/air` (main merged in first; a HANDOFF conflict, both sides' entries kept). Plan Mode, approved ("Sounds
good": the plan's recommendations taken as the owner's answers, written into the plan's asks): **no fog in battles**
in AIR-3 (fogit as before; a grid round the battle stage is a later item); **over budget on phones, cut in this
order**: fewer steps (10 to 8), then no lamps in fog, then a smaller grid; fogit's mist **steps aside inside the grid
only** (pushback on the plan's "`uMist` 0": the grid reaches 24 m, 16 on phones, and the camera sees about 36).
- The march (engine/post-effects.js `vol`) with the grid: it starts where the ray enters the grid's box (or the shafts'
  last 14 m, if nearer) and runs to the surface or out of the box, 14 steps (10 on phones). It reads the R8 3D texture
  at flat heights (`curveY` put back; repeat x/z, clamp y). Fog: 0.22 a metre at full density; the light it scatters is
  the haze colour (dimmer in shade and with the sun's brightness, so dark under the moon) + the sun through the
  shadow maps with the HG phase (shafts in the fog) + the lamps (`fogLamps`). Out: premultiplied, composited by the
  grade pass's existing `c*(1-a)+rgb` (the shafts' output in front of the fog's T). **Without the grid the march is
  the old one exactly** (same segment, steps and sums; checked by reading, the fog terms are 0).
- Its own gate (`fogMarchOn`, logic/fog-grid.js): a grid, not `BT` (battles, director frames: the train ride's
  `BT.hazeK` untouched), quality step < 3, `air.fogVolume` > 0.01, and not the debug "no post". It runs with no shadow
  map (`vis` returns 1, the stand-in depth bound) and with God rays / Lamps in the air at 0; the shafts themselves
  still need the shadow map. Rooms, caves and the bowl have no grid (the bowl calls the post with no `fog`): fogit as
  before.
- No double fog: the Frame block's new `vec4 uMistBox` (the grid's middle x, z, half size, on; 2288 bytes). Inside it
  fogit's low mist and valley mist fade out between 0.7 and 0.95 of the half size, and the march fades out over the same
  band (`FOG_EDGE`, `fogGridInside`). `fogGridFrame` moved before the light context, so a frame's mist and march agree.
- New `air` settings and dials (Air section, after Lamps in the air): `fogVolume` 1 ("Fog in the air"; 0 = the flat
  mist as before) and `fogLamps` 1 ("Lamps in the fog"); both 0 in PLAIN_LOOK.
- Debug log: `fogGrid.march`: on, or why not (battle, no grid, quality, dial, no post), steps, frames run, changes.
- Tests (fog-grid.test.mjs): the gate (off in battles, quality 3, no grid, dial 0; nothing about shadows or shafts), the
  box and the edge blend (the march's and the mist's shares add to 1), the ray/box twin (from above, clipped by the
  surface, missing, from inside, slanted), and the shader sources (`precision highp sampler3D`, flat heights, the
  edges, the mist stepping aside only when the march reads the grid). frame-block.test.mjs: `uMistBox` at 2272.
- Pictures: new tools/look-air.py (looks by hour, weather and `fogVolume`; `--phone`). Copperleaf, software drawing,
  in the session's scratchpad (not committed): clear noon matches the dial at 0 but for a faint near haze; dawn fog:
  banks over the low ground with sun shafts and shadowed columns through them; dusk and night fog: lamps and the
  fountain glow in it, the fog dark under the moon; phone (32 grid, 10 steps) the same look, a little softer.
  The first density (0.6 a metre) buried the square in fog weather: cut to 0.22.
- Verified: lint, typecheck, format, check:modules, unit tests 1335 pass; the smoke check 6 of 6 in 160 s (the in-game
  test's shader step: 35 shaders, 16 with the Frame block, all compiled); no page errors in the look-air runs.
- Risky: **the phone's frame times are not measured** (software drawing here says nothing): the owner's exported debug
  log after walking in fog (GPU `post`, and `fogGrid.march`) decides; over budget, the cut order above. The fog sits at
  quarter size with the plain blur, so it bleeds round edges (AIR-4's depth-aware blur). The grid's edge may show as a
  soft band where the march hands over to fogit (seen faintly on the phone shot, behind the square). In fog weather
  the look is heavy at dawn: the dial `fogVolume` tunes it. The shafts outdoors now step with the fog's spacing
  (same sums, noisier).
- Next: AIR-4 (edges and shadowed haze). Tag `air-3-done` for the owner.

  the other side: all of parts.css at the top of ui-kit.css, 619; per family .px 56, .pb 48, .pbar 73, .seg 44,
  .mon/.row 63, .chip 0. And nearly every one of the 48 !important really beat a screen rule. The owner chose (second
  question round): shrink it in place, move what moves cleanly, leave the rest for UI-9b.
- **Changed (one cause per commit, no change on screen):**
  - `tools/css-order.mjs`: the page's stylesheets in index.html order at a revision and now; lists each pair of
    declarations that can meet on one element and set the same property whose winner changed (!important,
    specificity, order), and each removed declaration nothing still beats (one on its own selector, or an !important
    on classes alone naming every class of its last compound). Matches declarations by a per-file alignment, then
    across files. Wary on purpose: a class meets a bare tag only where the code writes it on that tag or sets it
    unseen. Seen working on planted faults (.pb moved: 16 fights; a live .sec-h declaration removed: flagged; a dead
    .px one: passes).
  - parts.css: 70 declarations a later one on the same selector always beat; 14 (in parts, shell, walk-tab,

### Region map track WM-2 - the region grid (logic only) - 2026-10-27
Branch `claude/wm-2-region-grid` (from WM-1's branch). The owner's answers: places a path by Expedition (I 9-10, II
9-11, III 10-11, IV 10-12, V 11-12), a free place before the boss, so 2 towns at 9-11 places and 3 at 12; no filler
towns; the scrapyard counts as a route; side areas flipped too; the grid in the logic only until WM-3; 64 m cells.
- logic/run-map.js: `runMapRows` puts each mini-boss's town right after it (the leader first, the town its reward), a
  free row at least before each mini-boss and before the boss; `runMapLength` draws the run's places a path from
  rules.json `run.map.path` by Expedition and as many mini-bosses as fit within `run.map.towns` (runStartPlan calls it
  before the region, whose zones are fitted to those rows); rules without rows (rules.json's own) draw Expedition I's.
  The row after the landing always has two lanes. Every lane of the free row before a mini-boss is route-like
  (nodeTypes.json `routeLike`: route, rival, mini-boss, scrapyard), redrawn on 'map|road|row|lane' when not.
- The region grid: `RUN_GRID` (64 m cells, every place 2 x 1, within 3 cells of the landing's row), `runMapGrid` (a
  seeded layout search with backtracking; the landing's links east, lane 0, and north, lane 1; east, north or south,
  never west; no overlaps), each main node's `at` and `size`; `runGridSide`, `runGridOverlap`, `runLinkDir`. When the
  grid can't hold a map's lane switches, the map is linked again without them. About 0.2 ms a map. validRun checks
  `at` and `size`.
- **Playable until WM-3**: `row` stays a node's step (every link goes to the next step); runExits, the scenes and the
  bowl read rows and lanes as before, so a north link still leaves by the east side in the walk. mapgen.js, run-loop.js
  and the arenas untouched (WM-7 can run alongside).
- nodeTypes.json: town weight 0 (towns only after leaders), `routeLike`. rules.json run.map: `path`, `towns` for
  `rows`, `minibosses`. The short map (debug menu, Run Lab, self-test, run-test.js, check-fast) is 6 rows: landing,
  route, leader, town, route, boss.
- run-side.js: a side area's leader comes before its town too (`runSideTypes`, `runSideProblems`).
- data-checks.js: `dataRunMapRules` checks `path` and `towns` (every length fits); the region check uses the drawn
  lengths; `runMapProblems` adds overlapping footprints, a link across no shared edge or going west, the landing's
  ways on not north and east, a path with fewer than 2 route-like places before a town, places a path or towns on a
  walk outside the rules; `runMapSweep` takes `expedition` and reports places a path, the grid's size and links by way.
  run-rules-code.js lists the new rules in code. content-preview's leader values use the longest run (12, 3 leaders).
- Studio Run Lab: a region-grid view (the default; footprints on cells, north up, north and south links dashed), a
  Steps view (the old picture), an Expedition picker (map, sweep and logic panel; Play this seed plays Expedition I),
  the place's cells and its links' ways, the sweep's new figures, the path and towns fields for rows and mini-bosses.
  The Studio's GitHub check (run lab and rules card steps) moved to the new view and fields; the perks editor's picks
  read `towns`.
- **What follows from the rules**: at 9-10 places every free step is right before a leader or right after a town, so
  Expedition I runs have no stalls and few waystations (the waystation tests use Expedition V); runs hold about three
  times the route places they did, so more route trainers.
- Sim (100 runs, balance mode, before -> after): trained party (level 40, 3 at home) Expedition I won 90 -> 68, places
  7.4 -> 9.2, battles 19 -> 27, route trainers 1.7 -> 8.1, the estimate 15 -> 22 minutes; III 34 -> 32 won; V 19 -> 17.
  The untrained bot never reaches a town now (each is behind a leader); the town and stall sim tests use a party
  trained to 20.
- **Found, not fixed** (mapgen's, before WM-2 as after, at the same rates): about 1 run place in 25 gets a river note
  ("no way downhill"; old maps 11 of 256 places, new 12 of 320); about 1 route trainer in 75 faces a wall (mapgen's
  spot `face`; 3 of 179 before, 7 of 540 after). New maps met them on fixed test seeds: run-side-world's SIDEW1 ->
  SIDEW2 and run-world-real's RL7WORLD3 -> RL7WORLD6 (with comments), and route-trainer-spots' "faces a wall" is now a
  share (at most 3%) instead of none. A mapgen session should fix both.
- The paths sit a little north of the landing's row on average (the second lane is always the northern one); WM-4
  can centre the region on the bowl.
- Snapshots remade on purpose: run-map, run-start, run-world-real (the maps changed), check-data's planted rules (the
  planted `rows` became a bad `path`).
- Verified: lint, typecheck, format, check:modules, check:data, build; unit tests 1416 pass; slow tests all pass but

### Air track AIR-2 - the fog grid: a density grid round the player as an R8 3D texture, unread - 2026-10-26
Branch `track/air` (main merged in first: a conflict in AIR-1's Frame block, main's `uShFix` in the pad slot AIR-1
kept and both test blocks: resolved side by side, 2272 bytes; AIR-1's work merged before each push). Plan Mode,
approved. Nothing reads the grid yet (AIR-3), so the game's look doesn't change.
- New game/js/logic/fog-grid.js (the density as plain numbers, type-checked, in the logic worker's list) and
  game/js/walk/fog-grid.js (the texture, the uploads, the debug view), both on the game's and the Studio's pages.
  The split is mine: the plan named walk/fog-grid.js only; the logic folder is what keeps the maths testable.
- The density: each column's fog top is the mean ground on a ring about 6 m round it (8 samples), plus a layer of
  0.5-2 m (thicker in fog weather), lifted to the water level plus Mist height near water, plus a valley's mist below
  its level (`walkRenderer.valley` x the Valley mist dial), times a value noise (5 m, drifting with the wind, faster in
  storms). The amount: the scene's mist (scaled by the Low mist dial, as lighting.js does) + 0.85 x `environment.fog`.
  So a hollow fills to its rim, a hilltop's top lies below its ground (clear), none indoors (`sc.indoor` or `sc.room`).
- **Claim corrected**: the dawn mist isn't a separate input. environment.js folds it into `environment.fog` (the
  larger of the weather's fog and the morning mist), so the grid reads it once from there.
- The grid: 48 x 12 x 48 cells of 1 m, 32 x 8 x 32 on phones (`PHONE`, the user agent, as walk-view-gl.js). A ring in x
  and z: world cell (ix, iy, iz) is texel (ix mod nx, iy - oy, iz mod nz). **For AIR-3**: sample at
  `(x/(nx*cell), (y/cell - oy)/ny, z/(nz*cell))` with repeat in x and z, clamp in y (the texture's wrap modes are set
  so). The grid is in flat world positions (no `worldCurveDrop`). `fogGrid` holds `tex`, `G` (nx, ny, nz, cell, ox, oy,
  oz).
- The grid's floor follows the ground under you (4 cells below, 3 on phones). When it is 2 cells off, every row is
  refilled at once. The columns' heights are kept, and the ring's samples share heights by cell (a third of the
  reads). Uploads:
  - a step across a cell refills and uploads one slab (texSubImage3D, `UNPACK_ALIGNMENT` 1, then back to 4);
  - when the weather, mist, valley or water moves by more than 0.02, every row is refilled over a few frames (12 rows a
    frame);
  - otherwise one row every 4 frames, so the noise drifts without a seam.
- Not built indoors (the texture is freed), not updated in battles. The hook is one call after the water in
  `drawWalkFrameInner` (walk-view-gl.js), in the GPU counters' `other` pass.
- Debug: the debug menu (Tests and performance) has "Show the fog grid": the cells over 24/255 as see-through blocks,
  not saved. The debug log's report has `fogGrid`: the size, the heights read, the builds, refills, slabs and rows,
  the uploads, KB, ms per upload (the CPU's side of the call) and the fill times.
- Measured headless (software drawing, this container's CPU), Copperleaf (fixture town):
  - the first build: 48-cell grid 11.6 ms, 32-cell grid 4.7 ms (31 and 11 ms before the shared heights);
  - a slab: under 1 ms; an upload: 0.005-0.15 ms on average, at most 0.4;
  - a weather refill: about 1-2 ms a frame for 8 frames on the 48-cell grid.
  The phone's own numbers are needed: Export debug log after walking in fog.
- Tests: tools/test/fog-grid.test.mjs: a hollow fills, a hilltop stays clear (even in fog weather), none indoors (even
  with fog, mist, water and a valley), fog weather, water and a valley thicken it, the sizes, a step refills one slab
  and reads one strip of heights, and the rolled grid equals one built there.
- Verified: lint, typecheck, format, check:modules, unit tests 1320 pass. In a browser (fixture town, desktop and an
  Android user agent): the grid builds, a step uploads one slab, fog weather refills it, a room frees it, the blocks
  draw, no page errors. The smoke check passed 6 of 6, and its pictures were compared with a smoke run of AIR-1's tip
  (before AIR-2): the walk, team, guide, shop, profile, mast and run sheet match (under 1.5). phone-map and
  phone-opening-pick differ by when the picture was taken (the postcard still open; the starter card not yet up), not
  by the scene: a second run of AIR-1's tip against its first differs as much (opening-pick 77.7, battle 18.6). The exported phone debug log has `fogGrid`.
- Risky: the build happens in the frame that opens a place (about 5 ms on a phone grid here); the floor's refill on
  stairs and hills (density only, about 2 ms); the weather refill adds about 1-2 ms a frame for a few frames. 27 KB of
  texture (8 KB on phones). The Studio's walk views build it too (round `walkView.pl`).

### Air track AIR-1 - haze: follows the sky, RGB fade, height falloff, ray mist, sky glow - 2026-10-26

  the sky's three colours, `uHazeSky` (the place's haze below the horizon, leaning to the sky's gradient above it:
  `uFogCol + skyGrad(view) - uSkyLow`), `uHazeTint` (red lost a little faster, blue slower), `uHazeFall` (height

  mist from the same integral along the view, mixed with the point mist) and `uSkyGlow` (a broad lobe on the sun's
  side; `sunFog` stays the tight lobe). One GLSL `skyGrad` (`SKY_GLSL`) is used by the sky shader and `fogit`.

    index.json lines; roster.json rows 51-53 (kind `mythical` for Pseudonymph). No kit `parts` (optional; no kit
    art). Bios, notes and cries are Claude's drafts.

    useMove sets the user's type override (`ov`, as Soak does on the target) to the target's types for

### HD-2D audit fixes and smart light shafts (one session, not a phase) - 2026-10-26
Branch `ccr-6f3a4696-vl6nkg` (this session's own: a cloud session pushes only there; BRANCHES.md would call it
`art/hd2d-fixes`). Started from main b87b818d (phase 20 R2-R3 merged). The owner asked for an audit of the HD-2D
effects already in the game (three code reviews and a headless on/off run of 14 effects in Copperleaf), then a fix plan
and smart, cheap god rays. **Every look change is behind its own switch, off by default** (phase 20's rule), so nothing
changes until the owner turns them on after a phone check.
- What the audit measured (headless, Copperleaf, 640x480, the share of pixels each effect changes): vignette 51%, bloom
  26%, ink 26%, outlines 20%, lamps at night 20%, shafts 13%, AO 12%, ground bumps 6%, contact shadows 6%, DOF blur 5%,
  lamp shadows 4%, ground AO 4%; **god rays 0: engine.json sets `air.godRays` 0 and `air.cheapShafts` defaults to 0, so
  the game has no light shafts at all today**.
- Smart light shafts (`air.shaftPick`, Engine > Air, off): `logic/shaft-pick.js` (pure, `tools/test/shaft-pick.test.mjs`)
  picks the cheap shafts every 0.4 s from tree crowns, the gaps between them, the two sides of houses (old 3D buildings
  and low-poly models with windows) and a place's `shafts` list; scored by shade behind the beam's foot (crowns and
  houses as circles seen toward the sun), forward scattering (looking into the light), distance from you (the walk
  camera stands 36-58 m back; the range counts from you), never over you; at most 3/5/8 by quality step and a quarter of
  the screen together; a showing shaft holds unless another scores 1.3x; fades in and out over 1.2 s. Drawn as a soft
  streaked beam (the fx program's uGlow 2). Needs `air.cheapShafts` > 0 and god rays off (as D7). Graphics test: "Sun
  gap, smart shafts".
- The fixes, each with its switch (all off): Rays follow the light (`sun.followLight`: the walk view never passed the
  light's colour, and the moon kept a full-strength warm glare); Window light faces out (`lights.windowFacing`: window
  pools were cut on a fixed +z line, wrong for every turned house; the facing rides in uLC.w); Steady shadow edges
  (`shadows.steadyEdges`: the sun maps' eye sat 2 m off the light's line, so the texel snapping drifted, test in
  tall-ground-draw.test.mjs; and the soft edge's blocker search now reaches its filter); Lamp shadows hold
  (`shadows.lampFix`: distance-scaled bias for the perspective lamp maps, a lamp's pool takes its lamp's map, lamps
  high by height above the ground); Shaded tree cores (`world.treeCoreShade`: the 30% darkening solid-props.js worked
  out and never used); Occlusion follows the slope (`shadows.aoPlane`: both ways along a line in a harmonic mean, so a
  plane gives none); Feet shade on sky light only (`shadows.groundAOSky`); Lamp light on water (`lights.onWater`);
  Outlines follow the camera (`color.inkFollow`: ink melts with the blur and fades past the focus, it faded from 25 m:
  half strength on you at zoom 1); Even bloom (`color.bloomEven`); Half-float HDR (`quality.hdrHalf`, read at start);
  Steady light on far props (`quality.normalMips`); Fronts lit as their material (`world.frontMaterial`); Building
  bumpiness (`world.buildingBumps`, 0..3, 0 = off: bricks, planks and roof tiles from the sheet's own texels, on the
  old 3D buildings and the low-poly models; the hub's houses are models now).
- Fixed without a switch (artefacts, no look intended): the near ring's bump lookup stays inside its 16 m square (seams);
  the no-worker fallback bleeds picture edges too (`bleedEdges`, shared with the helper thread).
- The light block: its float padding slot is now `uShFix` (the shadow fix bits); the size and offsets are unchanged
  (frame-block.test.mjs knows the new member).
- **Risky**: the AO slope fix went through two wrong tries (a one-pixel slope was all depth steps at 40 m; a plain mean
  misreads planes) before the harmonic mean; headless it is within noise at zoom 1, brighter close up. Building bumps at
  the usual zoom read the sheet's half size (a texel is half a screen pixel there), so they are subtle; 1.5 shows on
  roofs and planks. Lamp shadows hold and Lamp light on water showed no change in Copperleaf at night (no case near the
  player); they compile and run.
- **Found, not changed (the owner's call)**: the screen AO fades out by 36 m, nearer than you stand at zoom 1 (reaching
  further darkened every grass blade's foot); props without `ppm` are at 34 px/m (scenery.json `ppu`), people at 42 and
  66.5, Billies on a 68 grid: an art rebake to reach 32; the sprite bump's +0.18 upward tilt may be meant.
- Verified: lint, typecheck, format, check:modules, unit tests 1297 pass, the smoke check 6 of 6, `check-fast --only=town` 4 of
  5 ("A run town's shop opens (UI-5): no shop with wares" fails on main 0ba64f10 too, not this branch's), every switch on at once in Copperleaf and a
  forest trail (no errors, every lit program builds with the light block), and headless on/off pictures for each
  switch. Not judged headless (phase 20's rule): how any of it looks or costs on the phone.
- Next: the owner on the Android phone and the iPad: Graphics test (Sun gap smart shafts; Shadow court, Lamp square,
  Meadow and Depth corridor now hold the new switches) and a debug log; then one commit per switch to turn on what
  stays. After that: cavity darkening from the same sheet, short self-shadows on the ground.

### Phase 20 R3, lane context (H1-H3, H5: the resource registry, freeing, memory by kind, warm-up) - 2026-10-26
Branch `track/renderer` (one of three R3 lanes: shadows, context, battle). Plan approved ("Continue") with my
recommendations: each owner drops its own handles on a restore and makes them again lazily (no stored rebuild per
object, which would have kept every mesh's and texture's data twice); the warm-up is on by default behind its own
switch (it doesn't change the look); the other lanes may create through the registry.
- Where the phase file, R1's notes and the code differed (checked):
  - Nothing needs deleting after a loss: the old handles died with the context (a delete on them does nothing). The
    real gaps were caches fooled by the restored context being the same object, and objects dropped without delete.
  - Already fine after a restore: the sprite instance buffer (keyed on `gpuState.quad`, new with each context), the
    rain batch's arrays (kept on the program; `gpuState.P` is emptied), the models' record buffer (flushed).
  - Not fine, found here: the cloth grid (`gpuState.gridGL === gl`) kept its dead buffer after a restore.
  - No program was ever replaced within a context, but a background compile whose program had been made on the spot
    meanwhile was dropped undeleted, a failed compile left its shaders and program, and no shader was ever deleted.
  - The walk set (WALK_SHADERS, POST_EFFECT_SHADERS) compiles in one blocking go in `ensureWalkGl`; the debug log
    already blames compiles ("compiling shaders", "finishing a shader"), and your Copperleaf hitches were blamed on
    the ground setup, not compiles: H5 doesn't touch the ground setup.
  - The precompile list (walk-view-gl.js `ensureWalkGl`, not webgl.js) already had every new instanced and batched
    program, the shadows lane's two included.
- Changed (one kind per commit; files of other lanes: create and delete lines only):
  - The known bugs: engine/light.js `frameBlockLost()` and walk/sprites.js `hideQueriesLost()`, run on every restore.
  - The registry (engine/webgl.js, "resources"): `gpuBuffer/gpuTexture/gpuVao/gpuFramebuffer/gpuMake(type, kind,
    bytes)`, `gpuSized`, `gpuFree` (a handle of an older context is only forgotten; one made outside it is deleted by
    its type), `gpuRetire` (freed two frame ticks later), `gpuOnRestore(name, fn)`, `gpuMemory()`. Entries sit in a
    WeakMap and never keep an object alive; one collected without `gpuFree` counts as "dropped" (a leak's sign).
    `gpuState.gen` goes up with every context and restore; caches compare it. The frame scheduler's tick calls
    `gpuFrame()`: retired objects freed, and a context that died before its lost event is marked lost at once.
  - Moved onto it: the engine's own objects (quad, stand-ins, samplers, pictures, canvases, normal maps, render
    targets, meshes, GPU timers); programs and shaders (shaders deleted once linked; duplicates and failures
    deleted); buffers and vertex arrays in prop-models.js (both halves: I moved the shadow maps' record buffer's
    create line, `MODEL_SHADOW_INSTANCES`), model-instances.js, sprite-instances.js, buildings.js, structures.js,
    solid-props.js, walk/effects.js (rain), walk/grass-build.js, engine/light.js, walk/sprites.js (queries); the
    ground (ground-textures.js, map-cache.js, ground-mesh.js, water-data.js: kinds ground and ring); the world map
    (world-bowl.js). Left on purpose: self-test.js's probes (they delete their own).
  - Restore: the walk view's drop (`walkViewGpuLost`) and the world map's (`worldBowlDropGpu`) registered with
    `gpuOnRestore`; the registry runs every drop first, then the walk view and the map are handed back.
  - H3, debug log: `gpuMemory` in the report (MB, objects and dropped objects by kind, the picture cap's own count,
    pictures trimmed, contexts made, `lateCompiles`: the names behind `pcl`), `gmb` (total MB) in every sample.
  - H5: `quality.warmUp` ("Warm up before showing", on): a place fades in once two frames have drawn behind its fade
    (at most 1.5 s), `mountWalkView`'s promise waits for it; a restore fades out and back in the same way.
  - Debug menu: the diagnostics test's note says 4-5 min on a phone (the R1 measure lane's note for this lane).
- Verified: lint, typecheck, `npm test` (1132), check:modules after every commit; the smoke check on every commit
  touching game/ (run from a worktree of the commit). New tests: tools/test/gpu-registry.test.mjs (counts, sizes,
  free, retire, generations, the early loss, owners' drops, render targets, meshes, programs). One headless crash check
  at low graphics (scratch script, no pictures compared), the town fixture: two forced losses, the world map with a
  loss, back to walk, a wild battle with a loss: every one restored and faded back in, **0 console warnings and 0 page
  errors after each loss** (R1's run had hundreds of "used but unbound" and getQueryParameter warnings), 0 objects
  dropped without being freed, `pcl` 0. Memory there (low graphics, 800 x 500): Copperleaf about 9 MB targets, 66 MB
  ground, 27 MB near ring, 15 MB pictures, 4 MB meshes; the world map adds about 20 MB pictures and 20 MB targets.
- Risky:
  - Shaders are now detached and deleted once their program links. It is the standard practice and passed the
    in-game shader test headless, but an old driver that misbehaves would show as a shader error in the log.
  - The warm-up holds a place's fade-in for up to 1.5 s on a device that draws slower than two frames in that time;
    turn "Warm up before showing" off if opening a place feels slower.
  - For the shadows lane: `shadowInstanceState.bad === gl` and `modelShadowState.bad === gl` (walk/shadows.js,
    prop-models.js) still compare the context, so a failure before a restore stays after it; compare `gpuState.gen`.
  - H2's `gpuRetire` is in place but no site needed it: WebGL keeps a deleted object alive until the commands using
    it are done, and no replacement found here was read after its old one was freed.
- To test on your phone (debug menu → "Lose the GPU context", wait 2 s, each one; send the debug log after):
  - Copperleaf by day: the town comes back whole and lit (buildings, trees, ground, water, shadows, lamps), fading
    back in; tap the button twice in a row, a few seconds apart.
  - Copperleaf at night (lamps and windows lit after the loss), and in the rain.
  - The world map (Map tab), then back to the walk view.
  - A battle at its move menu, and again with "Reuse battle rigs" on.
  - A run place (jungle) and a run town, with "Shadows in batches" and "Models in batches" on.
  - The Studio with `?glLose=12`: the battle preview with a walk scene open before 12 s pass.
  - In each debug log: `gpuMemory` (what each kind holds; `dropped` should stay 0), `lateCompiles` empty after a tour
    of the town, a route and a room (`pcl` 0), and whether opening a place feels slower with the warm-up.

    every 167 ms, attack and hurt every 83 ms, the face every 250 ms). Yet each rig was redrawn and uploaded on every
    frame: at 34 fps about 5 of 6 redraws repeated the last.

    their own sheets, tints are `source-atop` fills, positions snap to whole pixels.

### Phase 20 round 1, lane context (H-early): listeners once, the world map rebuilt on restore, a forced loss - 2026-10-26
Branch `track/renderer` (from 33115c7). Plan approved in Plan Mode. The owner's answers: the Studio is tested through a
URL flag; the button loses and restores by itself; the world map rebuilds only its GPU parts; the Frame block's stale
buffer goes to the light lane (asked again once it turned out to be on in the game: the owner passes it to them).
- Where the phase file and the code differed (checked):
  - Lines moved: the listeners were at engine/webgl.js 633-643, the world map's `initWebgl` call is world-bowl.js
    `worldMapCanvasGl`, the restore handler walk-view-gl.js `onGlContextRestored`.
  - How the listeners piled up: the walk view and the map share `#dio`, and `initWebgl` runs only when `gpuState.cv`
    changes; but the restore sets it to null, so every restore added one more pair (the second loss remounted twice).
  - The main gap: a restored context is the **same object**, so every `x.gl === gl` cache check still passed with dead
    handles (all of the world map's, light.js's Frame block, sprites.js's `hideQuery`).
  - The world map broke after a restore: its loop drew on `gpuState.cv`, null by then.
  - `buildingState.fac` holds canvases, not GPU objects (not tied to the context).
  - `quality.frameBlock` was on in the game at 33115c7 (game/data/engine.json set it `true`; settings.js's code
    default was false). Since the light lane's 73838b9 the switch is gone and the Frame block is always on.
  - A loss starts before its event: a frame drawn in between turned the buildings, models and solid props off for the
    rest of the session (their guards' fail flags). Found by the crash check below.
- Changed (one cause per commit):
  - Engine (webgl.js): `watchContextLoss(cv)`, the listeners once per canvas; a restore calls the walk view's and the
    world map's handlers.
  - Walk view (walk-view-gl.js `dropWalkGpuCaches`, every restore, shown or not): the ground caches, prepared views and
    ground job, basin, buildings', models', solid props' and structures' meshes, the last sun shadow map and its key;
    the three fail flags cleared so those try again. `npm run modules` added one generated `provide` line each to
    prop-models.js, solid-props.js and structures.js (additions only).
  - World map (world-bowl.js): `worldBowlDropGpu` drops every GPU copy (island, fine rock, falls, lagoon, mesh, sea,
    shadow map, lines, terrain maps, things, atlas, wall, sky) and keeps the work behind them; `worldBowlContextRestored`
    makes the programs again when the map is open.
  - H4: the debug menu's "Lose the GPU context" (next to the quality buttons) and `?glLose=<seconds>` (default 8) on any
    page, the Studio's too: `forceContextLoss()` marks the context lost at once, loses it and restores it 1.5 s later.
    The debug log says "context loss forced", "context lost", "context restored".
  - Tests: tools/test/context-loss.test.mjs (listeners once, restore order, the walk view's and the map's caches dropped
    and the map's CPU work kept, the forced loss).
- Verified: lint, typecheck, `npm test` (1061), check:modules, smoke on every commit. One headless crash check at low
  graphics (browser_check's LOW_GRAPHICS, scratch script, no pictures compared): Copperleaf lost twice, the world map,
  back to walk, a wild battle at its move menu, the Studio's battle preview with `?glLose=12`; each came back and drew
  again, one "context restored" per loss, no page errors, models rebuilt. The same run with a raw `loseContext()` (no
  early flag): the same.
- Left, with what the crash check still shows after a restore:
  - **Light lane (the owner passes it on):** engine/light.js's `frameBlock` cache keeps `gl` and `buf`, so after a
    restore it never makes its buffer again and every lit draw has no light buffer bound (hundreds of "used but unbound"
    warnings). Fix: on a restore, `frameBlock.gl = null` (for instance a `frameBlockLost()` export that the walk view's
    `onGlContextRestored` calls). Verified in the page: clearing it removes every one of those warnings.
  - Sprites lane (R2): sprites.js `hideQuery` keeps the old context's queries (`getQueryParameter` warnings, about 20
    per loss); its `hideQuery.gl !== gl` check doesn't notice a restore. Fix: drop `hideQuery.q` on a restore.
  - Round 3 (registry, H1-H3): nothing is deleted after a loss (the old handles are only dropped); the battle stage's
    own parts beyond the walk view (none found that hold GPU objects); programs never deleted; the texture budget;
    precompile jobs are reset by `initWebgl` already. A real loss's frames between the loss and its event still draw on
    the dead context (harmless now that the flags retry; the registry could check `gl.isContextLost()`).
- Risky: the fail flags now retry after every restore; a device whose buildings or models really fail tries once more
  per loss (logged again in the debug log). The world map keeps its CPU work: a GPU part this list missed would show as
  missing ground or things on the map after a loss.
- To test on the phone (debug menu → "Lose the GPU context", then wait 2 s):
  - The walk view in Copperleaf: the town comes back whole (buildings, trees, ground, water, shadows); tap it twice in
    a row, a few seconds apart.
  - The world map (Map tab), then back to the walk view.
  - A battle (debug menu → Battle it now), at the move menu.
  - The Studio: open it with `?glLose=12`, open the battle preview with a walk scene before 12 s pass.
  - The Frame block is always on now, so lit things may look wrong after a loss until the light lane's fix lands;
    that is the known leftover, not this lane's regression. Send the debug log of each.

Branch `ccr-bdf253b3-4vm5w6` (the session's own: the owner chose to work here instead of `fix/player-visibility`,
which didn't exist; one session's work, one PR). Not a phase: the owner asked for a system and approved the plan in
Plan Mode with these answers: all three layers (silhouette, see-through circle, a better whole-object fade); the
silhouette an outline in the colour of your top (lifted if dark); you and the one you talk to; the setting renamed
"Your outline when hidden". No tag (not a phase).
- What was there (TR-3, checked in the code): the silhouette and the rock's see-through circle only while ground cuts
  the camera's line (`rockK`); behind a house or tree on flat ground neither showed. A 0.4 fade written out twice
  (walk/sprites.js, solid-props.js): one test point, instant, props over 1.6 m, and **never the low-poly models**,
  which are Copperleaf's buildings (lab, shop, cottages: `M.model` with a door, not `M.build`).
- Changed (one cause per commit):
  - **logic/occlude.js** (new, tests occlude.test.mjs): `pictureCovers` (the cover test, moved first with no change),
    `hiddenEase`, `outlineColour`, `coverTarget`, `fadeEase`.
  - **Silhouette for anything that hides you** (sprites.js `drawPlayerSilhouette`): no `rockK` gate; an invisible first
    draw is an occlusion query (`ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED_CONSERVATIVE`), its answer `walkRenderer.hidT`, eased into `hidK`;
    pull toward the eye 0.8 m (was 0.6). Debug log: the camera line's `hidden`.
  - **Outline** (sprite shader `uGhostE`): the picture's edge whole, the inside dotted (`outlineFill`), in the top's
    colour (`lookOf`, the worn top's first colour, else the wardrobe's; looked up once a second). Engine > Camera
    `outline` (1 art pixel; 0 = the old dark blue tint), `outlineFill` (0.25).
  - **Talk partner**: while `talkBox.on`, the person or townsperson within 1.5 m of `walkRenderer.talkAt` gets the same
    outline in their own top's colour; not counted toward your `hidK`.
  - **See-through circle when hidden** (draw-common.js `rockUniformsFor`): on with `hidK` as well as `rockK`; the
    buildings' three shaders got ROCK_GLSL (the models, built on them, no longer add it). Engine > Camera `hideFade`,
    `hideSize` (0.3), `hideAmount` (0.7, capped at 0.85).
  - **Circle dither moved by (2, 1)** (walk-shaders.js `rockHides`): with the fades' own pattern, a picture both faded
    and in the circle lost every pixel, the query saw nothing and the circle flickered off (found in the pictures:
    lab, shop, a tree). Now at least 2 cells in 16 stay for any fade from 0.1 and circle up to 0.85.
  - **Whole-object fade** (walk/quality-cull.js `coverItems`, after culling): your feet, middle and head; to
    `coverFade` (0.4), halfway back while the circle is on; eased per placement (out about 0.25 s, back about 0.5 s);
    models and voxel props fade now (they read `it.fade`).

    the query, the talk partner and the circle; `tools/look-behind.py` (pictures, validation/behind/, ignored).
- Where the plan was wrong: an occlusion query that says "how much" needs `SAMPLES_PASSED`, which WebGL2 doesn't have;
  `ANY_SAMPLES` is yes or no, so the "minimum amount hidden" filter is the 0.8 m pull alone (a lamp post in front of
  you turns the circle on; it only cuts what is in front of you inside it). No `?fixture=behind`: the spots are found

    any palette shade and keep their colour: a ramp swap gave half-blue, half-orange tigers. So a kit Billie's form
    gets **its own baked look**: a kitBuilds.json recipe with the same parts and sizes in the form's colours, marked
    by a new `form` field and keyed by the form's species (rig `hughes_harbour0`), so the form draws its own sheet.

    through their coats, unchanged.

    **5.4** over 200 seeds, losing at the landing in about half of them - and the same on the branch point (5.6), so

### Test cleanup track, round 3 - TC-4: shared helpers, check-quick on fixtures and waits, the tiers - 2026-10-23
Branch `track/test-cleanup` (pulled with --no-rebase before every push). TC-4 items 1, 2, 5 and 6, over two sessions
(the first ran out of room). The owner said to make the recommended choices without waiting for plan approval. main
(RF-3, RO-1) merged in first. The track is done; the owner pushes the `tc-done` tag.
- Where the track file was wrong: software drawing is multi-threaded (one page keeps about two cores busy, two pages
  fill a 4-core container, a boot takes 25-65 s), so more browsers buy nothing; 13 check-quick steps already opened
  their own fixture page, only the 22 desktop steps replayed the start with `play()`. "About 10 min" for the full check
  and "1-3 min" for the fast check are not reachable on this hardware with every page drawn in software (below).
- **Item 1**: `tools/browser_check.py`, the shared helpers (serve on a free port, CLOCK, NO_ACCOUNTS, TEST_GLOBALS,
  LOW_GRAPHICS, `until` with an optional poke, `new_page` with extra init scripts, `open_game`, `console_text`, `log`,
  `frames`, `drawing`, `stand`, `go_scene`). check-fast, check-quick, check-ui-gallery, check-sound and
  check-studio-github use it; style-diff, look-blur, island-perf and island-shots import it; look-tall-ground still
  loads check-fast (TALL_SPOT), which re-imports the same names.
- **Item 2**: check-quick on check-fast's model. Each step is `def step(P)` on a Page opened by its first step at
  `?fixture=<name>` ('title' = the phone flow's real opening, None = no page). 13 pages in `--workers` browsers
  (default 2), longest first; `play()` is gone; QUICK_RENDER is an init script; a page error fails the step it came
  in; each page's boot is recorded (`boot` in results.json) and left out of the step's time limit. 93 of 95 sleeps
  became waits (`ui`, `drawn`, `look_at_me`, `bowl_drawn`, BOWL_OPEN, BATTLE_LEFT); two stay with comments. The
  battle, run and speed pages (battles/starters/battle weather, RL-8/Juniper/airship, postcards/running/settings)
  draw with check-fast's low graphics (their steps read state). The double/Alpha battles and battle music play at
  four times the animation speed.
- **Check fixes** (each its own commit; every one was the check, not the game): battle music's cue waits 20 s and the
  lost payout's jingle 40 s; battle music at 4x, since on a busy machine the throw came after the drums' 8 s fallback,
  which logs nothing; the Alpha foe level 12 (a level-6 Alpha fell to the first move and the catch was skipped);
  `go_scene` waits at least 60 s for a scene's first frames (Juniper's "black screen" after the RL-8 run); the
  postcard step loads the card's picture and stretches the card's 9 s timer while it checks it (the card had gone);
  RL-8 taps Take off again while the run sheet is still there (a lost tap); run map music waits for the map song
  (Run music's last check leaves the deadline song asked for) and puts the walk tab back even when it fails (its
  failure had taken Battle music with it); check-fast's CAM-2 encounter swoop waits 30 s and the orbit check resets
  the camera first (CI failed that pair once); check-fast's screens check taps a Billie sheet's tab again until it
  opens (a lost tap; that commit also carries check-fast's docstring times).
- **Fixed on main's behalf**: check-fast's "Play this seed" built its Node plan without the run's region (RL-R1), so it
  failed on main since #167 and on this PR; it passes the region now. check-data-text treats an event option's `need`
  as a condition, as it does an unlock's `when` (RL-12b's `team >= 2` stopped CI's smoke job); main's #173 made the
  same change (and reads then/intro as scripts), and the merge keeps main's file. main's #170 fixed the in-game test's two false
  failures the baseline run's selftest job hit (merged in).
- Tried and reverted: steps that share a fixture sharing a page (13 pages to 10) saved 66 s of 1338 and broke Run
  music, which needs the run's landing untouched.
- **Results** (a 4-core cloud container, one heavy check at a time):
  - Full check: 2455 s and 35 of 37 steps before (main, with other work beside it; round 2 measured 1872 s). Five
    full runs after: 1338 s (1 problem), 1272 s (the reverted page sharing, 3), 1217 s (1), 1259 s (3), and
    **1282 s with all 37 passed** on the last. Each problem was a check that lost a tap or waited too little on a busy

  - Smoke: **188 s**, 3 steps, no problems (budget 1-2 min).
  - Fast check: **677 s** on CI on dfbe76c (27 checks on 19 pages, 2 browsers, all passed); 665 s here (26 of 27: the screens check lost a tap on the Billie sheet; fixed, it taps again until the tab opens).
  - `npm test`: 20 s; lint, typecheck, check:modules clean after every change.
  - Why the 10-minute budget is missed: a desktop frame takes about 1.5 s in software beside another page, at a third
    of the resolution or with low graphics alike, and the game clock moves at most 60 ms a frame, so game-time waits

### Phone speed, calmer effects, five times of day - 2026-10-23
Branch `claude/new-session-yby9e8` (one session, restarted from main after PR #170 merged). From the owner's three
debug logs of 2026-10-23 (Android phone, iPad, Windows) and their ask: the phone runs badly, menus are sluggish, blur
and haze toned down ("don't drop the blur, make it more subtle"), a stylized time of day with about five times to tune
in the Studio, and more suggestions (tech and visual).
- What the logs say (checked in the code):
  - Android in Copperleaf: **1,770 draw calls and 27,400 uniform calls a frame** (iPad 1,050 / 10,000); **864 sprite
    draws against the iPad's 191**: a phone held upright keeps about 1,000 of 1,530 things in view (the iPad 230).
  - On Android Chrome a wait on the graphics process shows up as main-thread time, so the automatic quality judged every
    slow frame "main-thread bound", held the effects at step 2 and pushed the resolution back to 1 every second: the
    phone ran the whole session at full resolution, 17-27 fps.
  - Phase 20 says the Android phone is limited by pixels: with engine.json's quality.resolution 1.5 it draws the 1.6 MP
    cap, but the calls are now the bigger cost. Stage E (instanced sprites) is the real fix.
  - Menus on a phone (portrait, under 960 px): a CSS blur on the full-screen live 3D canvas, glass blurs of 10-18 px on
    top, all redone every frame because the world kept drawing at 24 fps behind full screens.
- Changed (one cause per commit):
  - Menus: the blur behind a phone's screens 1.5 px to 0.8 px (kept, at the owner's word); the world behind a full
    screen settles for 0.8 s, then draws once a second (a still canvas keeps its blurred backdrop); phone glass blurs
    halved through CSS variables (a no-op commit first: the fixed values became variables with today's values);
    Billie pictures redraw at most 20 times a second (their pose moves in 50 ms steps).
  - Walk: the automatic quality's step is a pure function (logic/quality-step.js, tests); on Android and iPhone a slow
    frame now takes steps 3-4 and then the resolution (not below 0.6), never raising it for "main-thread" time.
    New settings Quality > Skip tiny props (minPropPx, 3 in the data) and Small props' distance on phones
    (phonePropDistance, 48 m in the data; small props under 1 m fade out over the last 8 m; buildings never). The
    effects pass skips props outside the view, and fountains outside it draw no spray.
  - Engine data, calmer: depth-of-field blur 2 to 1, behind you 2.6 to 1.4, sharp band 0.62 to 0.8, colour fringes 1.15
    to 0.35, vignette 0.72 to 0.4, bloom 0.8 to 0.6, glare 0.9 to 0.6, saturation 1.2 to 1.1, mist 0.16 to 0.08.
  - **Five times of day** (logic/time-of-day.js, tests): engine groups todDawn, todDay, todGolden, todDusk, todNight
    (25 dials each: hour offset and blend, sky colours and amount, light colour and strength, fill and its colour,
    haze colour, amount and distance, mist, exposure, saturation, contrast, warmth, shadow strength, shadow and
    highlight tints, glow, lamps, stars). Dawn sits at sunrise, day 3 h after it, golden hour 1.4 h before sunset, dusk
    0.4 h after, night 1.8 h after (all move with the season); each look is reached over its blend hours, the one before
    holds until then. They replace, outdoors, the old dawn/dusk/night sky tints, warm sun and moon colour, night ambient,
    saturation, exposure, warmth and bloom terms, the dawn mist and the lamps; weather, a scene's own look and the
    player's dials stay on top; rooms keep their light. The colours are game data (engine.json); the code's defaults
    have none (the ui-lint ceiling on colours in game code). The Studio's Engine page lists the five groups and a bar
    under its moments: hour, weather, season, Play a day (24 h in 20 s) and which looks make up the light.
- Not done, with reasons:
  - Debouncing `save()`: the save is 2.3 KB (the log's saveBytes), a write is well under a millisecond; not worth a
    lost save.
  - A schema file for the looks: engine.json has none; the dials' ranges live in ENGINE_SPEC as for every other group.
  - The phone pixel budget (phase 20 D4) and quality.resolution 1.5 / shadowMap 4096 in engine.json: unchanged
    (phase 20 says ask first); the automatic quality now brings the phone down from them.
- Verified: lint, typecheck, unit tests (863) and check:modules after every commit; check:data; the Studio's 32
  sections open with no error (check-studio-github.py --only=sections); a scratch Playwright run of the Engine page:
  the five groups, the bar, 19:45 shows "golden 50% + dusk 50%", 23:30 "night 100%", Play a day sweeps; smoke (see
  below). The looks through a summer and a winter day printed from the data (night until ~4:30, dawn at sunrise, day
  from ~9:00, golden hour before sunset). **Not judged headless** (phase 20's rule): how the looks and the calmer
  effects look, and the speed. Please try on the phone and iPad and send a debug log.
- Risky:
  - The looks change the picture at every hour but midday; the starting values are my guess at "stylized". Tune them in
    the Studio (Engine > Time of day, with the hour bar).
  - On a phone the resolution can now fall to 0.6 when frames are slow: softer, but the frames should come.
  - Small props fade out 40-48 m away on phones: watch for things popping in a long street.
  - The world behind a full screen moves once a second: it may look still or stutter behind the glass.
- PR #170's follow-up (the full test's three false failures): headless, the whole in-game test went from three red
  steps to one, "Opening: falling across the Hollow Earth: the fall drew 1 frames" (software drawing late in an 11-minute
  run; it passed alone with 9 frames). Proposed fix, not made: run the fall for 6 s x selfTest.slow in the test.
- Suggestions for next (tech and visual, ranked): phase 20 stage E (instanced sprites: ~864 sprite draws to tens),
  stage F (instanced models and merged shadow casters: shadows are 200-400 draws), GPU-tier presets from the renderer
  string and a warm-up benchmark, invalidateFramebuffer after post passes and RGBA8 targets on phones, half-rate
  shadows and reflections on phones by default and lamp shadows for the nearest 1-2 lamps only; for the looks: a toon
  light ramp per look, coloured ink outlines per look, glowing windows and lanterns that follow the lamps (stage I2),
  painted cloud cards, fireflies at night, cheap god-ray quads at dawn and golden hour (stage D7); menus that redraw
  only what changed; the world map's idle water at 10 fps.

### Fix - the hub's "black screen" in the full quick check - 2026-10-23
Branch `fix/hub-frame-wait` (one session, docs/BRANCHES.md). The failure in RL-R1's long checks (PR #161's comment):
"Ground tiles, building plans and colours, rooms": `w:copperleaf* isn't drawing (black screen)`, under CPU load.
- Cause: the check, not the game. `go_scene` wanted 2 new frames within 30 s of a place opening. Once a minute the
  debug log takes its picture of the scene (`screenSnapshot`, `readPixels`), which makes the page wait for the software
  drawing to finish. That frame took 1.2-1.5 s on a fresh page (with or without 8-16 busy loops), but 16-23 s late in a
  14-minute desktop run (4 busy cores, or the unit tests looping beside it). One more slow frame in the same 30 s and
  the step failed. The screen was never black: the draw loop kept running (`frameScheduler.tasks.has('dio')`). On a
  phone's graphics chip that wait is a few milliseconds.
- Changed (tools/check-quick.py `go_scene` only; no game code, data or names): after 30 s without 2 frames, if the draw
  loop is still running it waits up to 60 s more and adds a note naming the slowest frame meanwhile. It fails only when
  the loop is gone ("stopped drawing: its draw loop is gone (black screen)") or fewer than 2 frames came in 90 s.
- Verified: a scratch probe on the hub, the old and the new `go_scene`. No new frame for 35 s: old fails with the
  PR #161 message, new passes with a note. The draw loop stopped (`frameStop('dio')`): both fail, the new one says so.
  "Ground tiles" and "Place views" pass with the unit tests looping beside them; the 12 desktop steps up to the hub
  step pass under load (the buddy lag in "Double and Alpha battles" is the known one, RF-2's entry). lint, typecheck,
  `npm test` (827), smoke (6 of 6). I could not get the natural failure itself on this machine: the stall reached
  20-23 s, short of 30.
- Risky: a step that goes through `go_scene` while frames are this slow now takes up to 60 s longer instead of failing.
- Found, not changed: tools/requirements-check.txt pins Playwright 1.56, which can't launch this machine's Chromium
  (1.63 works). And the frame scheduler (frame-scheduler.js `runFrameTasks`) drops a task for good when it throws, so
  one error in a walk frame would freeze the scene until it is mounted again. No sign of that here; worth its own look.
- Before merging: merge main again once RF-4 has merged, and run the checks again.

### Tooling - Repo admin workflow (tags and branch deletion for cloud sessions) - 2026-10-23
Branch `claude/optimistic-maxwell-vhge6s`. Not a phase: asked for by the owner so sessions can make tags and clean up
branches (the git proxy refuses both with HTTP 403).
- Changed: `.github/workflows/repo-admin.yml`, run by hand (workflow_dispatch). `create-tag`: a lightweight tag on a
  commit, names `legacy` or `<name>-done` only, an existing tag is never moved; on a `phase-*` tag it starts the Check
  workflow on the tag with `baseline=true`, since a tag made with GitHub's own token starts no workflows (a dispatched
  Check also runs the selftest job, which a pushed tag doesn't). `delete-branches`: never main, legacy, the default
  branch, archive/* or a branch with an open pull request; the run summary lists each branch's last commit.
  `dry_run` is on by default. docs/BRANCHES.md says to use it.
- Branch naming (owner's ask): docs/BRANCHES.md "Naming and long plans" (the kinds of branch and their names; a
  plan of several sessions lives on one `track/<plan>` branch named in its plan file, every session starts on it and
  checks it, the branch stays after its PRs merge) and a CLAUDE.md line pointing there. The workflow never deletes
  `track/*`. The old tip to turn on "Automatically delete head branches" is reversed: it would delete a track branch
  on every merge. Existing long branches (`sound`, `RL-10b`, ...) keep their names until their plans end.
- Risky: the workflow can delete branches and runs with `contents: write`. Anyone who can push could edit it on a
  branch and run that copy; only people with write access can run workflows at all. To limit it to main's copy, give
  the job a GitHub environment that only allows main (Settings -> Environments).
- Verified: actionlint clean; both scripts run against a stand-in `gh` (protected names, open PRs, missing branches,
  dry run, empty list, bad and existing tag names, the phase-tag Check start). Not run on GitHub yet: it must be on
  main first.
- Done after the merge (PR #146): dry runs of both actions on GitHub, then the `legacy` tag (0314a22) and the
  clean-up, 157 branches down to 22 (docs/BRANCHES.md lists what is left and why; each deleted branch's commit is in
  the Repo admin run summaries). Found: "Automatically delete head branches" is on (the owner should turn it off, see
  BRANCHES.md); `sound` holds SND-6, 13 commits, not merged and with no PR.

**The logic worker's messages (fixed; Phase 3's dashboard builds on them)**
- Page side: `logicAsk(fn, ...args)` in `studio/js/logic-client.js` returns a Promise of the value. It sends the
  Studio's data as it is now (`studioState.D` as JSON text, `_` keys left out); that text is the data version: the
  same text reuses the worker, other text ends it (its waiting asks reject with `replaced`) and starts a new one.
  `logicWorker` holds `state` ('off' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'failed'), `loadMs`, `error`, `made`.
- page -> worker: `{ kind: 'data', v, version, json }` once (GAMEDATA = JSON.parse(json), PB_VERSION = version), then
  `{ kind: 'ask', id, fn, args }`.
- worker -> page: `{ kind: 'ready', v, ms }` or `{ kind: 'failed', v, error }`; `{ kind: 'answer', id, ok: true, value,
  ms }` or `{ kind: 'answer', id, ok: false, error }`. An ask sent before the data loaded waits for it.
- What may be asked: `LOGIC_WORKER_FNS` in `studio/js/logic-worker.js`, name -> (modules) => function; the modules are
  `studio/js/logic-worker-modules.js`'s exports. To add runSim: export it there, add `runSim: m => m.runSim`. The
  worker loads game-data.js and every logic module in load-logic.mjs's order (a unit test keeps the list equal to
  game/js/logic/: a new or moved logic module must be listed there too) and stands in for the page's hooks as
  load-logic.mjs does (no Math.random seeding: the logic's streams are seeded).
- `runPreview(seed, { unlocks, map, tier })` (game/js/logic/run-preview.js) returns `{ seed, tier, unlocks, map,
  deadline, forecast, nodes: [{ wild: { lv, list }, foe, shop: null | [{ day, stock, relic }] }], relicOffers }`.

**T2.4 spike: what the logic touches outside a worker**
- game-data.js, rules.js, run-loop.js, battle-engine.js, run-scenes.js, run-start.js, run-map.js, relics.js and all
  they import (hooks.js, test-globals.js, util.js, rng, effects, fighters, battle-state, conditions, mapgen, parts,
  robot-math, meta-state, run-state, unlocks, weather): no `window`, `document`, `localStorage`, `navigator` or
  `location` while loading or running, except:
  - test-globals.js reads `window.PB_TEST_GLOBALS` and `location.search` inside a try: in a worker it is off;
  - util.js's `$` and `$$` default to `document`, but only when called (the logic never calls them).
- They need `globalThis.GAMEDATA` before game-data.js loads (it reads the tables once) and `PB_VERSION` (a new save's
  gameVersion), both set by the worker.

**Changed** (one cause per commit; two merges of the Phase 1 base)
- **T2.4** run-preview.js + test (equals the game's own path for 5 seeds x none/all/short); the worker
  (logic-worker.js, logic-worker-modules.js, unit test); logic-client.js and the Lab's "From the game's logic" panel.
- **T2.5** logic/run-rules-code.js (11 rules in code, snippet + unit test) and the "Run rules" card beside the map.
- **T2.6** logic/run-test.js (the address, unit test); boot.js: `?debug&run=` is a TEST_RUN that takes off through
  runTakeOff (runTestStart); the live channel carries rules, nodeTypes, relics, unlocks, items (applied only in a test
  run); the debug log's `state.run.unlocks`; the Lab's "▶ Play this seed"; check-fast step "Play this seed".
- **T2.3** data-checks.js runMapProblems / runMapSweep (after Phase 1's moved checks) + unit test (1,000 seeds, about

    still carry them and the game ignores them (decision 10).

  (`D/maps/<id>`, `D/lines/<i>`, `D/meta/<key>`, `D/<key>` for a value), one per rig (`R/<species>`) and `@order`.
  `last` is the parts, held once; a data step is `{ parts: { name: [before, after] } }`, null for an added or removed
  part. Bytes count 2 a character; data steps have their own 64 MB cap (`HISTORY_DATA_BYTES`). API names unchanged;
  art steps unchanged; a group's `snapshot` is the same diff. 11 unit tests (diffs, round trip, bytes, trim by
  bytes, mixed order, a group with a data diff, the counter).

  counted as the browser stores them (1 byte a character unless one is past U+00FF). Report format 2.

  51 maps the same objects (`===`); the undo's size with the three biggest edits.

- **Drafts (T1.1).** `studio/js/drafts.js` (new) and `game/js/logic/draft-record.js` (new, 4 unit tests).
  - Written to IndexedDB (`pb-studio-drafts`, one record per `owner/repo@branch`) 2 s after the last change
    (`updateTopBar` calls `draftSoon`) and when the tab is hidden. Holds only what is pending: the data files whose
    text differs from the loaded commit (`changedDataFiles`, index.json included, so deletions come back), the rigs
    when they differ from what loaded, each unsaved picture as a Blob (re-encoded only when its `_ver` changes), the
    base commit, the login, the time. No token.
  - `confirmStaged` writes at once: the draft goes when a proposal took everything, or keeps what changed meanwhile.
    A failed proposal leaves it.
  - Boot (github.js): sign-in → `draftOffer` (Restore / Later / Discard, before any data is read) → boot → `draftStart`.
    Restore sets `githubMode.baseP` to the draft's commit, so every read and the proposal use it and T0.2's question
    names files main changed since. The draft is applied all or nothing; undo starts empty. Later keeps the draft and
    writes nothing over it this session; Discard asks again, then deletes.
  - No IndexedDB (private window, blocked storage): the Studio works and the top bar shows "⚠ Not kept if the tab
    closes".
- **check-studio-github.py `drafts_checks`** (`--only=drafts`): restore of a data, a rig and a picture edit after
  `page.close()`; the restored draft proposes all four files and the draft goes; a failed proposal keeps it; main
  moved (the question says so, every read at the draft's commit, Propose names meta.json); Later; Discard; a browser
  without IndexedDB. With the restore turned off it reports 6 problems; as committed, 0.
- **T1.6.**
  - check-data: a `_` key in a data file listed by index.json is an error (F7). The rule is the first function of
    `game/js/logic/data-checks.js`, T1.3's module (2 unit tests; it is on the Studio page so the page lint test is
    happy).
  - TESTING.md: the unit tier is 628 tests in about 42 s here, over its 30 s budget.
  - ESLint now lints `tools/*.mjs` with the unit tests' rules: 0 findings, so no code changed.
- Docs: STUDIO.md "Unsent changes are kept in this browser", CHANGELOG.

**Where the plan doc was wrong or short**
- "Mirrors the ledger": there is no ledger since Phase 0; the draft is built from the same per-file diff Propose uses.
- "Different base: restore with the overlap warning" would put back main's older text in the shared files; restoring at
  the draft's commit avoids that (owner approved).
- T1.2's acceptance uses `fullMB`, which studio-test.js computes as `snapMB x 80` (an estimate). Session B must make
  it a measurement first. `updateTopBar` also stringifies the whole model on every call (`last === snapshot()`).
- T1.4: `check-quick.py --studio` needs `start-studio.py`, which is not in the repository.
- T1.6 `_` keys: only schema/ (`_help`) and legacy/README.json (`_world`) have them, neither listed in index.json.

**Verified**
- Unit tests 628 pass; lint, typecheck, `check:modules`, `format:check`, `check:data`.
- `check-studio-github.py --only=publish`: 0 problems (Phase 0's regression check). `--only=drafts`: 0 problems.
- A planted `_planted` key in meta.json: check-data names it.
- `check:fast`: 25 of 25 pass.
- `check-studio-github.py --only=sections,studio_test,publish,drafts`: 27 sections open, publish 0, drafts 0 (a write
  took 63 ms in that run). One problem: "the edit in rules did not come back with undo", the plan's F14, which Phase 0
  also saw on unchanged main; session B (T1.5) hunts it.
- **Not run:** the full quick check (planned at the end of Phase 1, session D) and the full chain of
  `check-studio-github.py` (it stalls at the story preview in this container, as noted in Phase 0).

**Risky**
- **Cost of a write.** A draft write takes 84-208 ms in headless Chromium here (stringify, split and format of the
  data, then IndexedDB), once per pause in editing. On a phone it may be a visible hitch. Measure on the iPad.
- **Two Studio tabs** on the same browser share one draft: the last to write wins. Each tab's own memory is unaffected.
- **Proposals add up.** After a proposal the data still differs from the loaded commit; an undo marks it unsaved and
  the draft then keeps those files too (as the next proposal would send them).
- **Not tested on a real phone or a real GitHub** (stand-in only). Manual check: edit, close the tab, reopen.

**Next**
- Session B: T1.2 (undo per file; first make `fullMB` a measurement) and T1.5 (F14).
- Owner decisions still open for C/D: T1.3 which Studio errors may block Propose (recommended: only what CI fails on);
  T1.4 CI time (recommended: yes); local mode and `--studio` (recommended: drop).

### Studio plan Phase 0 - Reliability and data safety on publish - 2026-10-22
Branch `ccr-81011a25-lf3exv`, PR #131. The PR also carries the plan itself,
`docs/plans/studio-roguelite-improvement-plan.md`: a review of the Studio at 5a30303d with Phases 0-6 and tickets.
The plan was approved in Plan Mode as written: tickets T0.1-T0.4 with a smaller design than the plan doc's "ledger".

**Changed** (one cause per commit; the test came first and failed on the old code):
- **check-studio-github.py `publish_checks`.** It runs on its own page with an injectable stand-in, after the main
  flow, or alone with `--only=publish`. The cases:
  - a 502 at blobs, trees, commits, refs and pulls (retry);
  - a proposal that can't be built;
  - a held send (a second Ctrl+S, and an edit made meanwhile);
  - every read at the loaded commit;
  - main moved on, sharing a file or not;
  - branch reuse and branch names;
  - a 401, with cancel or with a new token.

  On the old code it reported **14 problems**: art and rigs dropped after every failure, and a partial proposal sent.
  Now it reports 0.
- **`game/js/logic/publish-plan.js`** (4 unit tests): `publishConfirm`, `publishEmpty`, `publishOverlap`,
  `publishBranchName`.
- **`studio/js/studio-app.js`.** `saveAll` is now `checkBeforeSave` → `stageChanges` → `writeStaged` → `confirmStaged`:
  - Nothing is marked saved before the server answers.
  - Then only what is unchanged is marked saved: pictures are matched by `c._ver`, which `markArt` already bumps;
    data and rigs by their text.
  - `meta.artVersion` goes up in the sent text and is set in `D` on confirm.
- **`studio/js/github.js`.**
  - **One proposal at a time.** The batch is built whole before anything is sent; an error sends nothing.
  - **Pinned reads.** Everything is read at the commit main was on when the Studio loaded (`githubBase`), including
    rigs-next.js, which used to come from the deployed page and was then written back whole.
  - **Pinned proposal.** The proposal's parent is that commit. If main changed files the proposal also writes, a
    question names them (Propose anyway / Cancel).
  - **Branches.** Names are `studio/<login>-<date>-<time>-<4 letters>`. A branch left by a failed pull request is
    reused (PATCH), and a 422 on pulls finds the PR that is already open.
  - **Expired sign-in.** A 401 opens the sign-in card (now with Cancel) over the Studio, then resends the same
    changes. A new token replaces an expired one kept in the other browser store.
- **Docs.**
  - STUDIO.md: "Propose changes: what it does, and what happens when it fails".
  - Local mode is marked "not in this repository", in STUDIO.md and in the Studio's load-error text.
  - CHANGELOG.

**Where the plan doc was wrong or short**
- `artDirty` is read in about 12 places as "the unsaved picture", so it stays. The ledger became a stage plus a
  confirm-by-version-or-text.
- The local-mode path could not be tested: there is no server in the repository.

**Verified**
- Unit tests: 622 pass.
- lint, typecheck, `check:modules`, `format:check`.
- `check-studio-github.py --only=publish`: 0 problems.
- `check:fast`: 25 of 25 pass.
- The full `check-studio-github.py` stopped in `story_steps`:
  - First at `#scStoryOn`, then at the "Play from here" click.
  - The same step fails on unchanged origin/main in this container, at the wait for the game's tab. This is the known
    stall noted beside `--only`, not this phase.
  - Every other step was run with `--only`:
    - The publish checks, the UI steps, the uiTheme proposal and the self-test's restore all pass.
    - Two problems, both also on origin/main:
      - free camera "the ground under the pointer moved"; origin/main fails the same step alone in this container;
      - the self-test's Rules edit not coming back with undo. That is the plan's F14, seen on main during the review;
        the plan's T1.5 tracks it.
- **Not run:** the full quick check. It was stopped at the owner's word, so the next session starts without waiting
  for it.

**Risky**
- **Undo and confirm.** Undoing a change after it was proposed marks it unsaved again, as before; that is fine. A
  restore (undo) during a send can make data differ from the sent text, so it stays unsaved: the safe direction.
- **New requests.** GitHub mode now makes one extra request at load (the ref) and one or two at proposal time (the
  ref, and compare when main moved).
- **Tested only against the stand-in.** The API paths used are GitHub's documented ones: `git/ref/heads`,
  `compare/a...b`, `PATCH git/refs/heads/<branch>`, `pulls?head=owner:branch`. One real proposal from the Pages Studio
  is the owner's check.

**Next**
- Phase 1 (T1.1 drafts in IndexedDB first; then T1.2 undo per file, T1.3 shared checks, T1.4 Studio checks in CI).
- Tag `sr-0-done` is the owner's.

### Island track IS-1 - Orbit camera - 2026-10-22
Branch `claude/is-1-orbit-camera`, from IS-0's `claude/new-session-3qlesh` (PR #119, not merged yet: the owner started
wave 1 before `is-0-done`); the PR goes against main and shrinks once #119 merges. Ran beside IS-2, IS-3, IS-4 and IS-6a.
Plan approved in Plan Mode; the owner's answers: question 2, the camera **holds still on the summit** (your own turn
still works); question 3, the **sun stays put in the world**, with an Engine toggle to compare; the tree picture fix
in sprites.js done here.
- Changed (one cause per commit):
  - **logic/camera-orbit.js** (pure, unit-tested; on the game and Studio pages, for IS-6a's "Walk the coast"):
    `orbitYawAt` (the yaw that looks from you at `c`; 0 from the south, so the first view is today's), `orbitStart`,
    `orbitStep` (the lag as a time constant of `lag` s; inside `dead` the target holds; the yaw kept unwrapped so the
    easing always takes the short way past +/-180; trimmed back near 0 every 8 laps), `orbitStickYaw` (the joystick's
    frame, below), `orbitWalkStep` (a step taken round the middle: the part across the radius moves you along your
    circle), `wrapAngle`.
  - **walk/camera.js**: `orbitOf(sc)`: the orbit applies outdoors, not in a room, not in the Studio's free camera,
    with Engine > Camera > Orbit on. The base yaw is the orbit's and your turn (`walkRenderer.yaw`) is added on top,
    limited to the map's `turn` (`cameraTurnLimit()`). No scene clamps on the target while orbiting. Four spots that
    assumed a north view now use the base yaw (all equal to before at yaw 0, so every other map is unchanged): TR-3's
    ground-ahead for the rise, the lean ahead of you (`rw > rh ? 2 : 1`), the swoop's offset, `landmarkTilt`. A new
    scene, a cut (`camT` cleared, `opt.instant`) or a jump of over 8 m starts the orbit where it belongs.
    `walkRenderer.orbit` holds the state. A turn kept from a map with a wider limit (Copperleaf's 35) is clamped to
    the island's on arrival. The battle, cutscene and Studio cameras don't go through it.
  - **walk-view.js** (joystick and keys): on an orbiting island the stick walks by `orbitStickYaw` (plus your turn)
    and steps with `orbitWalkStep`; elsewhere it is unchanged (the camera's right).
  - **sprites.js**: `landmarkTilt(P, sc, yaw = 0)`; a tree's crossing picture fades by `|sin yaw|`, not `|yaw|`.
  - **Engine > Camera**: `orbit` (on) and `sunTurns` (off; on turns the sun with the camera in engine/light.js
    `sunLight`).
  - **Debug log**: the scene line's `orbit` (yaw, your turn, `hold` on the summit, `stickLocked`; degrees).
  - **check-fast's island step**: 8 places round the coast (the camera looks at the middle within 0.06 rad and aims
    within 4 m of you), the summit holds, the turn limit is 30 degrees, holding right goes an eighth of the way round
    and stays within 1 m of its 44 m circle with no yaw jump.
- Where the plan was wrong or short:
  - **The walk drift fix needed more than "steer by the target yaw"**: a step straight along the tangent still adds
    s^2/2r to the radius every frame (0.5 m a lap at 20 fps running, more on slow frames), and last frame's target is
    stale by a frame. The stick reads the way to the middle from where you stand now, and the step goes round the
    middle: a lap ends on its circle to 1e-13 m in Node (8, 20, 60 fps), 45.0 m of 45 in the browser.
  - **Crossing the summit holding up** would bounce you at the dead zone's edge with any stick frame that follows
    the orbit (the way to the middle flips half a turn as you step out the far side). So while the stick is held its
    frame stays locked from the moment you are inside the dead zone until you let go. Leaving the summit northward
    holding up, you keep walking north while the camera swings round behind you (lag 0.6 s); push again and up is
    toward the middle.
  - Shadows and culling needed nothing: both work from the camera's own view (screen rays, the frustum), not a
    facing. The shadow map stops 6 m past the scene, where only sea is.
  - The sun was already fixed in the world (Engine > Sun > angle); question 3's "fixed" option was free.
- Verified: unit tests 577 (10 new); lint, typecheck, check:modules, format:check, check:data (143 files);
  check-fast 22 of 22 (the island step 48 s with two browsers); smoke all fine. In a 390 x 760 page with full graphics
  at 8 angles: the camera looks at the cone from every side, no page errors, TR-3's rise and rock fade 0 everywhere
  on the ring; a full lap holding right (194 s of software drawing) ended at 45.0 m. Copperleaf's camera is unchanged
  (no orbit; every changed spot is identical at yaw 0).
- **Found for IS-3 (not fixed: water is IS-3's)**: from the west and east the far sea floats over the near ground.
  The `flatFar` skirt (walk/ground-mesh.js ~775) is four quads of 4 corners each, and the world's bowl curve
  (`curveY`, about 0.0012 x d^2 past 70 m from the scene's middle on test_island) lifts each corner by its own
  distance. The west and east quads run 300 m long, so their inner edge at x 0 is lifted ~10 m (the corners at z -90
  and 210) and the water sheet covers the sand and the ring up to ~20 m in. The north-facing camera never stood past
  those edges, so it never showed. Fix: cut the skirt into a grid (e.g. 10 m cells) so the curve bends it like the
  ground. From the south and north it looks right.
- Risky:
  - The stick's locked frame (above) is new behaviour; worth a feel on the phone at the summit.
  - With "Sun turns with the camera" on, the shadow cache redraws every frame you turn (the sun moves): a
    comparison setting, not for the phone's frame times.
  - studio/index.html gained a script line next to camera-rise.js; IS-6a may add the same line (keep one when merging).
  - Phone frame times at 8 angles are IS-9's; nothing here measured a phone.
- Next: IS-3 (the sea skirt above), IS-6a can call `orbitStep`/`orbitStart` for "Walk the coast", IS-5 when IS-2
  lands. Tag `is-1-done` is the owner's to push (after `is-0-done`).
